---
title: "Who lives here"
subtitle: "Demographics and identity, by the numbers and in residents' words"
---

```{r setup}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
age <- read_csv("data/age_profile.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ind <- read_csv("data/indicators.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
theme_ncs <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top",
        plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))
```

The census and the residents give two different pictures of Adamsville. The census shows a young, working-class, mostly Black community with high poverty and heavy use of transit. The residents I interviewed described a quiet, older, close-knit place. I think both pictures are accurate, and the difference between them is important for planning.

Most figures on this page are for NPU-H, the 16,000-person planning unit that includes Adamsville and the surrounding subdivisions that residents also call "Adamsville." I did not rely on the city's smaller statistical area for Adamsville (NSA H02, shared with Oakcliff) because it has only about 3,000 residents, so its estimates carry very large margins of error (population 3,013 ± 1,911). All figures are American Community Survey (ACS) 2020–2024 five-year estimates compiled by the Atlanta Regional Commission (ARC) from U.S. Census Bureau data.

::: {.stat-row}
<div><b>16,248</b><span>NPU-H residents (± 2,904)</span></div>
<div><b>88%</b><span>Black, non-Hispanic (Atlanta 45%)</span></div>
<div><b>$53,658</b><span>median household income (Atlanta $85,652)</span></div>
<div><b>44%</b><span>of children below the poverty line (Atlanta 23%)</span></div>
:::

```{r age-chart}
#| fig-cap: "Share of residents by age group, NPU-H and City of Atlanta. Source: ARC, ACS 2020–2024."
#| fig-height: 5.5
age |>
  mutate(age_group = factor(age_group, levels = rev(age_group))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(npu_h, atlanta), names_to = "area", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(area = recode(area, npu_h = "NPU-H", atlanta = "City of Atlanta")) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, age_group, fill = area)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NPU-H" = "#d2493c", "City of Atlanta" = "#8a918d")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "More children, fewer adults aged 20 to 44 than the city") +
  theme_ncs
```

```{r dot-chart}
#| fig-cap: "NPU-H compared with Atlanta. Red bars show the NPU-H margin of error. Source: ARC, ACS 2020–2024."
#| fig-height: 5.5
ind |>
  mutate(indicator = factor(indicator, levels = rev(indicator))) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = indicator)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = pmax(0, npu_h - npu_h_moe), xend = npu_h + npu_h_moe, yend = indicator),
               linewidth = 4, color = "#d2493c", alpha = 0.25, lineend = "round") +
  geom_point(aes(x = atlanta), shape = 21, size = 3.5, fill = "white", color = "#4a5450", stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = npu_h), size = 4, color = "#d2493c") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, 75)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Red = NPU-H, open circle = City of Atlanta") +
  theme_ncs
```

## What the numbers say

NPU-H is 88 percent Black, compared with 45 percent citywide. Its median household income ($53,658) is about 63 percent of the city's ($85,652), and 30 percent of residents live below the poverty line. For children the figure is 44 percent. Housing is cheaper than in most of Atlanta (median home value $214,316 against $439,600), but many households still struggle to pay for it. 57 percent of renters and 45 percent of mortgage-holding owners spend 30 percent or more of income on housing. Over a quarter of households have no vehicle, and the average commute is 34 minutes, nearly eight minutes longer than the city average.

```{r change-chart}
#| fig-cap: "Selected NPU-H indicators, ACS 2006–2010 vs. 2020–2024. Source: ARC."
#| fig-height: 3.8
ind |>
  filter(!is.na(npu_h_2010)) |>
  select(indicator, `2006–2010` = npu_h_2010, `2020–2024` = npu_h) |>
  pivot_longer(-indicator, names_to = "period", values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, reorder(indicator, pct), color = period)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = indicator), color = "grey70", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2006–2010" = "#8a918d", "2020–2024" = "#d2493c")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL, title = "Poverty, vacancy and rent burden fell since 2010") +
  theme_ncs
```

Since 2010, the estimated population has grown from 14,988 to 16,248, poverty fell from 33 to 30 percent, and vacancy dropped from 19 to 12 percent. Median household income roughly doubled in current dollars (from $26,807), which probably reflects both recovery from the foreclosure crisis and the arrival of higher-income households. In Adamsville's core (NSA H02), about seven in ten households rent, although that estimate is much less certain (± 21 points).

## Swipe the map: 2006–2010 vs. 2020–2024

Drag the white handle left and right. The left side shows census tracts in 2006–2010; the right side shows the same tracts in 2020–2024. Choose the measure with the buttons, and hover over a tract to see both values and the margin of error. The red outline is NPU-H; the dashed outline is Adamsville's statistical area (NSA H02).

```{r swipe-data}
#| output: asis
cat("<script>window.TRACTS = ", paste(readLines("data/tracts_acs.geojson", warn = FALSE), collapse = ""), ";</script>\n", sep = "")
cat("<script>window.NPUH = ", paste(readLines("data/npu_h.geojson", warn = FALSE), collapse = ""), ";</script>\n", sep = "")
cat("<script>window.NSA = ", paste(readLines("data/nsa_h02.geojson", warn = FALSE), collapse = ""), ";</script>\n", sep = "")
```

```{=html}
(function(){

  L.tileLayer("https://services.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Canvas/World_Light_Gray_Base/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}", {maxZoom: 16, attribution: "Esri, HERE, Garmin, OpenStreetMap contributors | Data: ARC, ACS"}).addTo(map);
  map.createPane("leftPane"); map.createPane("rightPane"); map.createPane("topPane");
  map.getPane("topPane").style.zIndex = 450; map.getPane("topPane").style.pointerEvents = "none";
  var breaks = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50], cols = ["#fff5eb", "#fdd0a2", "#fd8d3c", "#e6550d", "#a63603", "#5e1f02"];
  function col(v){ if (v == null) return "#ccc"; for (var i = 0; i < breaks.length; i++) if (v < breaks[i]) return cols[i]; return cols[cols.length - 1]; }
  var key = "pPopPov", names = {pPopPov: "Poverty rate", pRenterOcc: "Renter households"};
  function tip(p){ return "<b>Tract " + p.GEOID.slice(5) + "</b><br>" + names[key] + "<br>2006&ndash;2010: " + p[key + "_e10"] + "%<br>2020&ndash;2024: " + p[key + "_e24"] + "% (&plusmn; " + p[key + "_m24"] + ")"; }
  function layer(pane, suffix){
    return L.geoJSON(window.TRACTS, {pane: pane, renderer: L.svg({pane: pane}),
      style: function(f){ return {color: "#fff", weight: 1, fillOpacity: 0.8, fillColor: col(f.properties[key + suffix])}; },
      onEachFeature: function(f, l){ l.bindTooltip(function(){ return tip(f.properties); }, {sticky: true}); }}).addTo(map);
  }
  var left = layer("leftPane", "_e10"), right = layer("rightPane", "_e24");
  L.geoJSON(window.NPUH, {pane: "topPane", style: {color: "#c2412f", weight: 3, fill: false}}).addTo(map);
  L.geoJSON(window.NSA, {pane: "topPane", style: {color: "#1c2422", weight: 2, dashArray: "6 5", fill: false}}).addTo(map);
  var range = document.getElementById("swipe-range");
  function clip(){
    var nw = map.containerPointToLayerPoint([0, 0]), se = map.containerPointToLayerPoint(map.getSize());
    var x = nw.x + map.getSize().x * range.value / 100;
    map.getPane("leftPane").style.clip = "rect(" + [nw.y, x, se.y, nw.x].join("px,") + "px)";
    map.getPane("rightPane").style.clip = "rect(" + [nw.y, se.x, se.y, x].join("px,") + "px)";
  }
  range.addEventListener("input", clip); map.on("move zoom resize", clip); clip();
  function restyle(){
    left.setStyle(function(f){ return {fillColor: col(f.properties[key + "_e10"])}; });
    right.setStyle(function(f){ return {fillColor: col(f.properties[key + "_e24"])}; });
  }
  document.querySelectorAll(".swipe-tools button").forEach(function(b){
    b.onclick = function(){ key = b.dataset.k; document.querySelectorAll(".swipe-tools button").forEach(function(x){ x.classList.toggle("on", x === b); }); restyle(); };
  });
  var lg = ["under 10%", "10&ndash;19%", "20&ndash;29%", "30&ndash;39%", "40&ndash;49%", "50% or more"];
  document.getElementById("swipe-legend").innerHTML = lg.map(function(t, i){ return '<span><i style="background:' + cols[i] + '"></i>' + t + "</span>"; }).join("");
})();
</script>
```

*Source: Atlanta Regional Commission, American Community Survey 2006–2010 and 2020–2024 five-year estimates by 2020 census tract. Tract estimates carry wide margins of error; read patterns, not single values.*

## Two stories about age

::: {layout-ncol=2}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What residents said
Resident A: "definitely a lot of long term residents, aging population." Resident B: people on her street are "like 55, 60 years old and over," and some are "starting to go into nursing homes or unfortunately passing away."
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## What the census shows
28 percent of NPU-H residents are under 18 (city: 17 percent), and 14 percent are 65 or older (city: 12 percent). Adults aged 20 to 34 are just 20 percent (city: 31 percent). 15 percent of households moved in before 1990, more than twice the city rate.
:::
:::

Both residents live among owner-occupied single-family homes, where long-time owners have aged in place. Much of the area's child population lives elsewhere, in rental apartments and rented houses; the master plan, for example, discusses keeping the Fairburn Gordon Apartments at the crossroads (City of Atlanta & TSW, 2020, p. 90). One possible explanation is that the homeowners who attend NPU meetings see an aging street, while many of the renting families who make the census numbers look young do not come to those meetings.

## Identity: contested from outside, protective from inside

Resident B said that people from outside "look at this area and think that it's a bad area," especially around Fairburn Road and MLK. A stray bullet hit her family's car in 2026 while her young daughter was inside. Even so, when she described the neighborhood she talked about quiet, wildlife, and neighbors who "treat you like family." One elderly neighbor took in the family's cat when her son turned out to be allergic, and the children still visit it.

::: {.voice .b}
"When you drive to the neighborhood, you'll be like, are there even people here? Because it's so quiet."
<span class="who">Resident B, interview, October 19, 2026</span>
:::

::: {.voice}
"It's right between like industrial, Fulton Industrial, and the city. It's like a sweet spot."
<span class="who">Resident A, NPU-H volunteer, interview, October 16, 2026</span>
:::

Both residents talked a lot about nature, including Wildwood Lake, the creeks, deer, herons and "lots of trees." This is close to the Civic Club's 1955 wish to preserve "the rural qualities we cherish." Residents also use "Adamsville" loosely for the area around the interstate exit, including subdivisions the city counts as separate neighborhoods, and the 1977 NPU-H plan already grouped Adamsville with Boulder Park, Fairburn Heights and Carroll Heights. In practice, the name works more as a regional identity, tied to the exit sign, the skating rink and the recreation center, than as a line on a map.
